The row the policy table is missing

docs/adaptive-pane-ux.md says: "App.tsx declares eighteen dockable component types. The per-view policies below cover twelve of them; Taxonomy assistance, Error log, Tab history, Sparsity, Text Analysis and Text Entities also inherit the shared measurement." Touchpoints, Inspector and Details each have a row in that table. Text Analysis has none. This is the row, in the published vocabulary, at the published thresholds.

ViewExpandedNarrowShallowPreserve
Text Analysis One action row above the editor: Auto, match state, presentation switch, View in Graph, overflow Same row; secondary actions overflow by measurement in a stable order Help sheet closes and every remaining pixel goes to the editor Text, caret, selection, scroll position, Undo history, Auto state, presentation and settled highlights

No threshold of this file's own. The action row does not break at a width; it measures itself and moves what does not fit into the overflow, in one order that never reshuffles. Fluent's toolbar guidance, already cited by that document, is the source for that. So the only numbers in the stylesheet are 600, 400, 239, 210 and 180, all published.

Why nothing is underlined

A rule under every match turns a page of text into a page of marks, which is the opposite of what a highlight is for. So the fill carries the signal alone, and each of the twelve tints is tuned to 1.40 against its own page, six per theme, computed rather than eyeballed. That floor is this file's own: there is no published figure for a highlight ground, and the tints here previously ran as low as 1.13, which is a wash you have to hunt for rather than a field you see. Raising it to 3.0, the figure WCAG uses for a graphical object, is one token edit away and would make the editor considerably louder.

Exactly one mark survives: a one pixel outline on the match the caret is sitting in. That is the one you are about to open, so it is a focus affordance rather than decoration, and it is never on more than one match at a time. Matches that moved with an edit and have not been reanalyzed lose their hue instead of gaining a mark, which holds their luminance so the field stays as visible and the text on it keeps its contrast.

Copy this rendering supersedes

docs/text-analysis.md, edited this morning, carries the old name in two sentences:

"Live analysis is on by default and runs matching after a 60 ms typing pause."

"Turning Live analysis back on analyzes any outstanding edits immediately."

Replace with Auto in both. The switch's accessible name is Auto, analyze while typing, so the shorter face does not cost a screen reader the meaning. Nothing else in that document is overruled: the 60 ms pause, the settled highlights moving with the text, the state surviving restart, and the Summary sharing one tab are all implemented here as written.

Known limits of this rendering

Axiom uses Monaco and this file cannot, so highlights are a backdrop rendered in register behind a real text surface. Typing, caret, selection, Undo and scrolling are genuine; a Monaco decoration API would replace the backdrop without changing anything above. Details, Add entity and the graph are separate views, so reaching them reports what it would do rather than faking the destination. The ontology is fourteen entities taken from the capture's own highlights, which is what makes the before and after comparable; it is not Axiom's matcher.

15 matches counts occurrences, not entities. The capture carries exactly fifteen highlighted spans over fourteen distinct entities, because Marketing matches twice, so the number in your own screenshot settles it.
